sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2

sources.verified_against: GoogleChrome/web-vitals@400d019, src/onLCP.ts, onINP.ts, onCLS.ts, onTTFB.ts
sources.supports: LCP good ≤ 2,500 ms, poor > 4,000 ms; INP 200 / 500 ms; CLS 0.1 / 0.25; TTFB 800 / 1,800 ms.

sources.title: Text size in translation
sources.verified_against: w3c/i18n-drafts@59e5e64, articles/article-text-size.en.html
sources.supports: Translated length relative to English, by source length — up to 10 characters 200–300 %, 11–20 180–200 %, 21–30 160–180 %, 31–50 140–160 %, 51–70 151–170 %, over 70 about 130 %.

sources.title: Recover from validation errors (pattern)
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting the pattern page (the page itself was not reachable)
sources.supports: Validate on submit; do not validate when the user moves away from a field; keep answers, add an error summary with focus, show messages next to fields; use novalidate.

sources.title: Error validation (pattern)
sources.publisher: CMS Design System (US Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services)
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting the pattern page
sources.supports: Validation on submit for most cases; instant validation only where answers are not obvious or fields are hard to complete.

sources.title: Digital Identity Guidelines, Authentication and Lifecycle Management (SP 800-63B-4)
sources.verified_against: Secondary summaries of the final revision (the NIST site was not reachable)
sources.supports: Passwords at least 15 characters when used alone (8 when part of multi-factor authentication); accept at least 64 characters; no composition rules; no periodic forced changes; check against breached and common passwords.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines and design tips (hit targets)
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting Apple's design tips page
sources.supports: Controls of at least 44 × 44 pt; the visible control can be smaller than the tappable area.

sources.title: Material Design accessibility (touch targets)
sources.verified_against: Secondary sources citing Material's touch-target guidance
sources.supports: Touch targets of at least 48 × 48 dp, with the visible element allowed inside a larger target.

sources.title: Automated accessibility testing (audit of tools against 142 known issues)
sources.publisher: UK Government Digital Service, cited by the DWP Accessibility Manual
sources.verified_against: DWP Accessibility Manual and GOV.UK guidance (search results)
sources.supports: The best automated tools found about 30–40 % of 142 known issues on a deliberately inaccessible page.

sources.title: Automated testing coverage report
sources.verified_against: Deque press releases (2021, 2022)
sources.supports: Automated tests covered about 57 % of issues by volume across about 2,000 audits; a vendor figure measured by issue count, not by success criteria.

sources.title: Response Times — The 3 Important Limits (Usability Engineering, ch. 5); after Miller (1968)
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting the chapter and Miller (1968)
sources.supports: 0.1 s feels instant; 1 s keeps the flow of thought; 10 s is the limit of attention, beyond which progress feedback is needed.

sources.title: The Economic Value of Rapid Response Time (IBM GE20-0752)
sources.publisher: W. J. Doherty and A. J. Thadani, IBM
sources.verified_against: IBM-hosted copy (figure titles only) and secondary accounts
sources.supports: Productivity rises sharply when system response is under about 400 ms (the "Doherty threshold").

sources.title: The Elements of Typographic Style (3rd ed., pp. 36–37)
sources.verified_against: Secondary sources quoting the book
sources.supports: 45–75 characters per line for single-column printed text, 66 as a common ideal.

sources.title: A mathematical model of the finding of usability problems (INTERCHI '93)
sources.publisher: J. Nielsen and T. K. Landauer
sources.verified_against: Secondary summaries (CACM 2012 "Sample size in usability studies")
sources.supports: Problems found ≈ N(1 − (1 − λ)^n); with the average λ ≈ 0.31, five users find about 85 % of problems on average. Later studies found 55–100 % for groups of five (Faulkner 2003), so treat five as a per-round minimum for one user group, not a guarantee.

sources.title: System Usability Scale benchmarks
sources.verified_against: Secondary sources citing the 500-study analysis
sources.supports: The average SUS score is about 68 (50th percentile); scores are not percentages.

sources.title: First-click studies (Bob Bailey and Cari Wolfson)
sources.verified_against: Searched; no primary or reliable secondary source found
sources.supports: Only the direction is used: a correct first click strongly predicts task success. The often-quoted 87 % versus 46 % is not stated as fact.

sources.title: Inline validation in web forms (A List Apart, 2009)
sources.verified_against: Searched; the 22 % figure appears only in uncited summaries, and later studies report more errors with validation on leaving a field
sources.supports: Not used for any default. Recorded so the old claim is not reintroduced.

sources.title: Label placement in forms (UXmatters, 2006)
sources.verified_against: Searched; secondary sources report findings favouring left alignment for scanning, and the "top-aligned is fastest" claim is disputed
sources.supports: Not used as evidence. Top-aligned labels remain the default for other reasons (narrow screens, translation, design-system practice).

sources.title: Classic HCI laws (Fitts 1954, Hick 1952, Miller 1956, Cowan 2001, Gestalt principles, Iyengar & Lepper 2000, Kurosu & Kashimura 1995, Kivetz et al. 2006)
sources.supports: Qualitative principles only (target size and distance, choice count, memory limits, grouping, choice overload, aesthetic-usability, goal gradient). No numeric threshold in the skill depends on them.

sources.title: Color vision deficiency
sources.publisher: MedlinePlus, US National Library of Medicine
sources.verified_against: Search results quoting MedlinePlus; consistent with Birch (2010, Eye) and a 2025 pooled analysis
sources.supports: Red–green color vision deficiency affects about 1 in 12 males and 1 in 200 females of Northern European ancestry; rates are lower in other populations.

sources.title: SwiftUI and UIKit API documentation (Font, DynamicTypeSize, accessibilityReduceMotion, UIFontMetrics)
sources.verified_against: Apple developer documentation pages for Font.system(size:weight:design:), Font.custom(_:size:), Font.custom(_:fixedSize:), View.dynamicTypeSize(_:), Text.init(_:tableName:bundle:comment:), Image.init(_:bundle:), Image.init(decorative:bundle:), EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion and UIFontMetrics
sources.supports: Font.custom(_:size:) scales with the body text style; Font.custom(_:fixedSize:) does not scale with Dynamic Type; dynamicTypeSize(_:) limits Dynamic Type within a view; accessibilityReduceMotion reports the Reduce Motion setting; UIFontMetrics makes custom UIKit fonts scale; Text with a string literal is looked up for localization; Image(_:) is a labeled image and Image(decorative:) is ignored by accessibility.

sources.verified_against: Apple developer documentation pages for asking permission, UNAuthorizationOptions.provisional and UNNotificationInterruptionLevel
sources.supports: The system prompts only the first time an app requests authorization, and later requests do not prompt; ask in a context that explains why; provisional authorization delivers quietly to Notification Center until the person keeps or turns off notifications; interruption levels passive, active, time-sensitive (breaks through notification controls) and critical.

sources.supports: Android 13 (API 33) adds the POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission and notifications are off by default for new installs; apps targeting 12L or lower get the dialog automatically, usually at startup; request it from a user action or after users know the app, explaining why.

patterns.name: Ask only what you need, and mark optional fields
patterns.rule: Know why you ask every question and ask only for information you really need. Add '(optional)' to optional fields; never mark mandatory fields with asterisks. Make clear why each question is asked.

patterns.name: Check answers before submitting
patterns.rule: Show a check-answers page just before the confirmation for small to medium transactions (one per section for long ones), so users see everything they entered and can correct it before submitting.

patterns.name: Confirm completion and say what happens next
patterns.rule: End a transaction with a confirmation page that gives the reference number, what happens next and when, contact details, and links to what users are likely to need next.

patterns.name: Validate on submit, then guide the fix
patterns.rule: Validate when the form is submitted, not when the user leaves a field. Show the page again with the answers kept, add 'Error:' to the page title, move focus to an error summary at the top, and show each message next to its field. Use novalidate instead of browser validation.

patterns.name: Help users create strong passwords they can manage
patterns.rule: Let users paste passwords, avoid overly strict or confusing constraints, and keep resets secure; strict rules push people to weak, reused passwords or to give up.

patterns.name: One honest page for unexpected problems
patterns.rule: Use the same page for all unexpected problems, log every error and fix it quickly, show the page only briefly, and switch to a 'service unavailable' page when a fix will take time.

patterns.name: Empty states that say why they are empty
patterns.rule: Distinguish first use (welcome, explain the feature, one primary action that starts it), temporarily empty (say why, given the feature) and error (summarize the problem, give a recovery path, no playful graphic). Use one primary action; a secondary 'Learn more' link is optional.

patterns.name: Specific, non-technical error copy
patterns.rule: Describe the problem as specifically as possible in the user's terms ('Form could not be submitted. Some required fields were empty.'). Avoid vague 'There was a problem', obscure error codes, and internal infrastructure detail.

patterns.name: One saving model per form
patterns.rule: Start with explicit saving; never mix automatic and explicit saving in one form. Keep the user's data in the form when saving fails, warn before leaving with unsaved changes, and do not auto-save text inputs, checkbox or radio groups, or native selects.

patterns.name: Show that work is happening
patterns.rule: Always indicate loading so users do not assume a silent failure. Prefer components' built-in loading states; use determinate indicators for waits of about 3 seconds or more; keep animation subtle.

patterns.name: Degrade gracefully and say so
patterns.rule: Never conceal that something is wrong. When only secondary parts of a page fail, render the page with those parts degraded; when a primary experience fails, show an error page instead.

patterns.name: Disclose progressively, without losing context
patterns.rule: Use progressive disclosure sparingly, keep the user's point of focus, pair disclosure icons with text, and do not confuse it with navigation.

patterns.name: Pick the message component by message type
patterns.rule: Classify messages as system updates, feedback on a user action, or awareness, and choose the component by prominence (banner for system and page-level messages, inline messages for form feedback).

patterns.name: Error messages that fix the problem
patterns.rule: Explain what is wrong and what to do, be specific (exact numbers, dates, the user's own data), avoid jargon such as 'invalid', do not over-apologize, place the error next to what needs fixing, and offer a one-step solution when there is one.

patterns.name: Disabled, read-only or hidden: choose deliberately
patterns.rule: Disabled removes interaction and is skipped by screen readers; read-only keeps the content readable and announced; hidden removes the option entirely. Pick by whether users need to see and understand the value.

patterns.name: Notification persistence matches importance
patterns.rule: Inline notifications persist until resolved or dismissed; toasts without actions may disappear on their own; actionable notifications persist until the action is taken; modals are for critical information that must block the task.

patterns.name: Dialogs for short, focused tasks
patterns.rule: Use dialogs for short tasks or urgent, task-relevant information; choose modal only when the user must respond before continuing, and non-modal otherwise.

platforms.name: iOS (SwiftUI, UIKit)
notes: `Text("Save")` with a literal is a `LocalizedStringKey`: SwiftUI looks it up in the string catalog. Hard-coded strings are not a defect by themselves; check that a catalog exists and covers them.
`Image("hero")` takes its accessibility label from the asset name. Check the name reads well, or use `Image(decorative:)` for decoration.
Targets are 44 × 44 pt; a smaller visible control is fine when `.contentShape` or padding gives it a larger tappable area.

platforms.name: Android (Jetpack Compose, Views)
notes: Material 3 components (`Button`, `IconButton`, `Checkbox`…) reserve 48 × 48 dp through `minimumInteractiveComponentSize()`; custom `clickable` elements do not.
Text sized in `sp` follows the user's font size; `dp` and `px` do not.
Colors and strings defined in theme files (`Color.kt`, `colors.xml`, `strings.xml`) are expected; probe hits there are not drift.

platforms.name: Flutter
notes: `IconButton.tooltip` is also its accessible label: an icon button without one is unnamed for screen readers.
`kMinInteractiveDimension` is 48 logical pixels; Material buttons meet it, `GestureDetector` and `InkWell` children do not by default.
`textScaleFactor` is deprecated in favour of `TextScaler`; both appear in older code.

platforms.name: React Native (and Expo)
platforms.detect: a package.json that depends on react-native or expo
notes: `allowFontScaling` defaults to `true` on `Text`; turning it off, globally (`Text.defaultProps`) or per element, ignores the user's text size.
`role` (or the older `accessibilityRole`) and `accessibilityLabel` are not set by `Pressable` and the `Touchable*` components; add them when the content is not plain text.
Web probes (`references/codebase-recon.md` §3 to §6) still apply to style objects and copy.

probes.look_for: Screens and overlays for the surface map.
Text that ignores Dynamic Type. Text styles (`.body`) and `.custom(_:size:)` scale; `.system(size:)`, `fixedSize:` and UIKit fonts without `UIFontMetrics` do not.
A cap on Dynamic Type. Acceptable on compact chrome; a defect on body content.
A tappable view that is not a `Button`. VoiceOver gets no button trait unless `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)` is added, and there is no pressed state.
Asset images. Meaningful ones need a readable label; decorative ones `Image(decorative:)`.
Accessibility work in the code. Zero hits in a custom UI is a strong signal for A11Y-32.
Colors outside the asset catalog or theme. They do not adapt to dark mode or increased contrast.
Animations; compare with ios-reduce-motion.
Reduce Motion handling. Zero hits while large or looping animations exist is a finding.
Content extended under the notch and home indicator. Fine for backgrounds; a defect for text and controls.
Loading, empty and refresh states.
Screens and overlays for the surface map.
Text sized so that it ignores the user's font size.
A custom clickable without `role` or `onClickLabel`. TalkBack announces no role; prefer a Material component or pass `role = Role.Button`. Check its size too.
An image or icon hidden from TalkBack. Right for decoration; a defect on an actionable icon.
A size under 48 dp. Only matters on a custom tappable element; icons inside Material buttons are fine.
User-facing text not in `strings.xml`.
Colors outside the theme (`Color.kt`, `colors.xml`). They bypass dark theme and dynamic color.
Edge-to-edge and keyboard insets. Zero hits on a recent target SDK means content may sit under system bars.
Custom back handling; check that system back still goes back and never loses work silently.
Loading and refresh states.
Screens and overlays for the surface map.
Text scaling turned off, often app-wide in a `MediaQuery` override.
A cap on text scaling. A low maximum (under about 2) on body text is a defect.
A custom tap target. It needs `Semantics(button: true, label: …)` or a button widget, and 48 × 48.
probes.counter_example: IconButton(onPressed: open, tooltip: "Close", icon: const Icon(Icons.close))

probes.look_for: Icon buttons; each needs `tooltip:`, which is also its accessible label.
Images; each needs `semanticLabel:` or `excludeFromSemantics: true`.
User-facing text not in the localization files (ARB).
Colors outside `ThemeData`. They bypass dark mode and the color scheme.
Reduce Motion handling. Zero hits while custom animations exist is a finding.
Safe areas and keyboard insets.
Loading, error and refresh states; check each builder handles `hasError`.
Screens and overlays for the surface map. With expo-router, the files under `app/` are the routes.
Text that ignores the user's text size, per element or globally.
Tap targets. Each needs `role` (or `accessibilityRole`), a label when the content is not text, and 44–48 points or `hitSlop`.
Images; meaningful ones need `alt` or `accessibilityLabel`.
Content hidden from screen readers. Check nothing meaningful or actionable is hidden.
User-facing text not in the message catalog.
Reduce Motion handling. Zero hits while custom animations exist is a finding.
Safe areas and keyboard handling.
Loading, refresh and empty states.
